Formulation
- Summary: Adult with acute onset of a severe, unilateral posterior-left headache (new for patient) with family history of migraines. No red-flag features documented (no fever, vomiting, visual disturbance, focal neurological signs, rash), and initial simple analgesia (ibuprofen) provided limited relief. Symptoms cause functional impairment at work. Protective factors include partner support and appropriate health-seeking behavior. Plan focused on stepped analgesia, rest/hydration, safety-netting and re-assessment if symptoms persist or worsen.

Mental Health Care Plan Details

Principal Problem: Acute severe left occipital headache
- Patient Goal(s):
  - Reduction/resolution of headache pain
  - Return to usual work functioning
- Clinical Goal(s):
  - Symptom improvement within 24–48 hours of applying recommended measures
  - Identification of any red-flag symptoms requiring urgent assessment
- Actions (Patient):
  - Take recommended analgesia as advised (stronger analgesic recommended by clinician — name not documented; dose/route/frequency not documented) regularly with food
  - May take paracetamol in conjunction with the recommended analgesic (dose/route/frequency not documented)
  - Rest and maintain good hydration
  - Monitor symptoms and seek care if pain worsens or new symptoms develop
- Actions (Clinician/GP):
  - Advised stronger analgesic (name not documented) to be obtained from pharmacy
  - Advised paracetamol may be used concomitantly
  - Safety-net advice given: return or call back if worsening pain, new symptoms (fever, rash, vomiting, neck stiffness), or recurrent similar episodes
  - If not improving within 1–2 days or if recurrent, reassess and consider further investigation or referral (plan to discuss next steps)

Secondary Problem: Functional impairment at work due to headache
- Patient Goal(s):
  - Resume normal work activities
- Clinical Goal(s):
  - Restore ability to perform work tasks once headache controlled
- Actions (Patient):
  - Rest as needed; attempt analgesia and hydration; consider short-term reduction in workload if feasible
- Actions (Clinician/GP):
  - Provide advice on symptom management and follow-up; consider further assessment if persistent symptoms impacting function (sick note or occupational advice not documented)

Patient Education, Emergency Care & Relapse Prevention
- Education Given: Yes. Topics Covered:
  - Analgesia options and to take stronger analgesic regularly with food (name/dose not documented)
  - Paracetamol can be taken with the analgesic
  - Importance of rest and hydration
  - Red-flag symptoms requiring urgent review (worsening pain, fever, rash, vomiting, neck stiffness, recurrent episodes)
- Early Warning Signs of Relapse/Worsening:
  - Increasing pain severity, new fever, rash, vomiting, neck stiffness, visual changes, focal neurological symptoms, recurrent similar headaches
- Coping Strategies:
  - Rest, hydration, use of recommended analgesics, seek prompt reassessment if symptoms do not improve

Consent, Coordination & Review
- Patient Consent to Plan: Yes (patient agreed to advised management and follow-up)
- Copy of Mental Health Care Plan Given to Patient: Not recorded
- Other Mental Health Professionals Involved in Patient Care: Not recorded
- GP Acknowledgment (if completed by other MH Professional): Not recorded
- Review Date: Reassess if not improved within 48 hours or sooner if red-flag symptoms develop; patient advised to call back after trying pharmacy-prescribed analgesia
